To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RG-rich RNA binding domain of FMRP is part of a beta-sheet structure that can be perturbed by mutations in the conformation switch residues, and that the extent of FMRP methylation is affected by these mutations.
FMRP is methylated by a PRMT1/3-dependent process that is influenced by residues encoded by exon 15.
FMRP arginines 507 and 513 are not directly modified but rather influence arginine methylation by altering the structure of the RNA binding domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of FMRP arginines by the 5'-N terminus of exon 15.
the molecular mechanism of fragile X mental retardate protein (FMRP) arginine methylation in the N-terminal RGG box, and how this modification affects FMRP binding to RNA.
how the FMR1 gene product, FMRP, is regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformational change in Ex15c is a major contributor to the loss of arginine methlyation, but that other residues in Ex15 are also involved.
the conformational switches in FMRP play a critical role in the arginine methylation of the RGG box, which is important for the function of FMRP in RNA metabolism and transport.
the conformational change in the N-terminus of FMRP, which involves the switch residues, is a prerequisite to arginine methylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ex15c N-terminus is not a substrate for PRMT1 or -3 in the context of FMRP and that the conformational change in the switch is important for methylation of arginine residues encoded by the exon 15 RG-rich region.

the RG-rich exon 15-encoded region can be methylated in vitro, but in vivo the extent of arginines in the RGG box are not methylated, likely because of the conformational state of the protein and/or its interactions with other cellular factors.
the Ex15c N-terminal residues are in an unfavorable conformation for PRMT1 and PRMT3, and that the conformational change induced by phosphorylation at S 500 is required for the methylation of Ex15c.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformational change that occurs when the conformational-switch is phosphorylated may be a prerequisite for the arginine methyltransferases to gain access to the RG-rich region.
the conformational state of the N-terminal domain of FMRP can influence the extent of its arginine methylation.
the conformational change in the switch region is important for methylation of arginines within the RG-rich region.
